errors.text: The hypothesis treats oxygen as a contaminant that must be reduced below 500 ppm, whereas the target process deliberately retains approximately 1.0 wt.% oxygen for interstitial strengthening while controlling alpha-HCP formation.
It replaces ink extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, and long-duration vacuum sintering with a high-pressure hot-extrusion operation that is not part of the target method.
It omits the required 1400 °C, 18 h vacuum sintering treatment, titanium-sponge oxygen getter, and water quench from 1500 °C.
It does not reconstruct the sequential Ta-to-Nb-to-Hf/Ti/Zr hydride decomposition and associated in-situ alloying mechanism.
The proposed Al-Zr precipitation mechanism is compositionally inapplicable to the stated Al-free powder mixture.
The falsification threshold of greater than 100 ppm oxygen is internally inconsistent with the proposed initial specification of less than 500 ppm.
The cited evidence does not support the specific hydride-decomposition temperatures, extrusion pressures, heating rates, cooling rates, DBTT reduction, or yield-strength improvement claimed.
